Q: Why doesn't my svg in react-native show any shadow? A:

This is not really a coding fix, but before you could make the shadow a radial gradient object of the same shape as opposed to a shadow in the design.

Q: How to exclude a project from CICD on Azure DevOps? A:

Basically, you can pass the ExcludeFoldersFromDeployment as a parameter to MSBuild. Combining that with the SkipExtraFilesOnServer does the trick.

/p:Configuration=Debug
/p:DeployOnBuild=True
/p:DeployTarget=MSDeployPublish
/p:MsDeployServiceUrl=OurDevWebServer/msdeployagentservice
/p:AllowUntrustedCertificate=True
/p:MSDeployPublishMethod=RemoteAgent
/p:CreatePackageOnPublish=True
/p:DeployIisAppPath=umbraco_TestSite
/p:IgnoreDeployManagedRuntimeVersion=True
/p:SkipExtraFilesOnServer=True
/p:ExcludeFoldersFromDeployment="media;App_Data\Logs;App_Data\preview"
/p:IncludeSetAclProviderOnDestination=False
/p:AuthType=NTML /p:UserName=

OR

Use an MS Build project file. Create an MSBuild project file from scratch

And the at the build solution step in VSTS, select or type the project file path instead of the solution file. You will have to remove it down the road though. The maintenance tasks tend to be hard and counter-intuitive whenever the code base grows quickly. Visual Studio will not warn you if you have build errors (like obsolete path) in the MS Build project file.

Q: Maven test compile does not find class in classpath A:

For me you have a strange maven setting somehow.

Assume we have following structure

src\main\java\Foo.java                                               
src\test\java\sub\optimal\mavenexample\AddressSearchFieldsTest.java

Foo.java

class Foo { }

AddressSearchFieldsTest.java

import org.assertj.core.api.AbstractCharSequenceAssert;
public class AddressSearchFieldsTest { }

class UrlParameterStringAssert extends
    AbstractCharSequenceAssert<UrlParameterStringAssert, String> {
    UrlParameterStringAssert(String s) {
        super(s, UrlParameterStringAssert.class);
    }
}

using your pom.xml following goal will be executed by mvn clean compile

# from the log output
maven-compiler-plugin:2.3.2:compile (default-compile)

and produce the following class files

target\classes\Foo.class

the goal default-testCompile (as you mention) is executed for example by mvn clean compile test

# from the log output
maven-compiler-plugin:2.3.2:testCompile (default-testCompile)

and produce the following class files

target\classes\Foo.class
target\test-classes\AddressSearchFieldsTest.class
target\test-classes\UrlParameterStringAssert.class

You should check why your mvn clean compile tries to compile the test class files.

Q: Sorting by AM/PM time A:

My ActivityTime column is currently a string with HH:MM:SS AM/PM format

This is a deeply flawed schema design. Thanks to internationalization/localization and time zone issues, strings are almost always among the worst possible methods for handling date/time and numeric data. This is a significant source of bugs, as well as worse for performance. Never NEVER NEVER store date/time or numeric values as strings.

BigQuery has both Time and DateTime types. Use them. It's far more efficient to parse input values to these types at create/update time than it is to reparse values over and over at read time, plus you'll have fewer bugs and do faster and more accurate date math.

Using strings can also subtly create MASSIVE performance impacts in the case where you may even need to parse every row in a table in order to accurately compare the stored values with an input or value from another table/column, even when the query only needs a few rows for the results. If things are already set with a date/time, no conversion is needed.

You really only ever want to deal with this stuff as strings at the last possible moment before showing it to a user or exporting it for another system.
